title: Understand stages and jobs
summary: Stages can group pipeline jobs in an order such as build then test. Jobs in one stage may run in parallel when runners are available.
introduction: Stages can group pipeline jobs in an order such as build then test. Jobs in one stage may run in parallel when runners are available. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Stages can group pipeline jobs in an order such as build then test. Jobs in one stage may run in parallel when runners are available.

blocks.code:
Stage 1: build
  Job: create app files
Stage 2: test
  Job: unit checks
  Job: accessibility checks
blocks.title: Understand stages and jobs

blocks.text: The plan places build before the test stage. The two test jobs may run at the same time. Features such as needs can change dependencies in real pipelines.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Explain why a test needing build output must wait for it.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Do not assume listing jobs in a file always makes them run one after another.
For more detail later, use this [GitLab further reading](https://docs.gitlab.com/tutorials/).

seo.title: GitLab: Understand stages and jobs
seo.description: Learn about understand stages and jobs in GitLab. Follow a small example, understand the result, and practise with a clear question.
